q: What kind of projects do you take on?
a: The studio focuses on three main types of work: custom marketing sites, internal tools and dashboards, and AI-powered assistants that sit on top of your existing data and docs. Everything is designed as one connected system rather than separate, one-off pieces.

q: Do you only build websites, or also AI and data systems?
a: Web is one pillar, but not the only one. Projects often combine a marketing site or product UI with data reporting, automation, or an internal chatbot. Pure AI/data work is also possible if there’s already a clear interface or workflow in place.

q: What does a typical budget look like?
a: Most web projects fall between the Starter and Growth ranges shown above, while AI and data pilots (for example, an internal assistant or a focused dashboard) tend to sit in the Bespoke range. If you are not sure where your project lands, use the booking form and we can calibrate together.

q: Can we start small with a pilot?
a: Yes. A lot of AI and systems work starts with a scoped pilot: one use case, one team, and clear success criteria. From there, the system can be extended across more data sources, interfaces, or teams if it proves useful.

q: We’re not technical. Is that a problem?
a: No. The studio is used to working with non-technical founders, marketing teams, and operators. The process focuses on how your business runs day-to-day, then turns that into clear flows, interfaces, and systems without requiring you to make technical decisions.

q: How do you handle AI and data privacy?
a: AI features are designed so that sensitive data stays under your control. That can mean using private models, careful scoping of what is searchable, or routing parts of the system through your existing security and governance processes.

Most projects involve a short discovery, a clear written proposal, and then a build phase with regular check-ins. You will see key decisions as they are made, rather than being handed a black box at the end.

Yes. Some clients prefer a clean handover with clear documentation, while others choose a light ongoing arrangement for improvements, new features, or additional data and AI use cases. Both options are available and can be discussed after the initial build.

q: What if we only need a small site or update?
a: Smaller, well-defined projects can still be a good fit as long as there is enough scope to add real value—such as tightening the structure, improving performance, or preparing the site to support future AI or data work.
